Explicitly checks all five anti-cheat rule categories: forbidden build-tool files/lockfiles/Dockerfiles, >1M binaries, and CSP-inline patterns (unsafe-inline/eval, localStorage, document.cookie, on*=) — showing a mapped model of the verifier's stated checks.

Validates a broad Mastodon endpoint surface against wire shapes (instance, timelines, verify_credentials, oauth apps/introspect, notifications, bookmarks, lists, reports, admin) and returns to edge cases as they surface — ETag cache validators (74), idempotency key (99), scopes — indicating an ongoing working model of the contract.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5: it extracts the hard constraints (vendored-lib hashes/paths, anti-cheat file rules, CSP), forms a working Mastodon API model, and validates it across dozens of endpoints. It reaches into level 8 by probing the environment (Python/pip/offline), touching all five anti-cheat rule categories, and confirming the hash-pin/canary detail rather than assuming. It stops short of 8+ because there is no explicit enumeration of the 19-gate categories and the protocol research is thin (two searches), so the API depth is inferred from validation rather than documented reconciliation — landing at a 7.
